{"id":"ENG-2346","uuid":"a9972593-2a3e-438c-8689-a65eacc24912","title":"Ignore unsupported placeholders when constructing Obsidian node titles on import","description":">>> ## Problem

* Obsidian node titles support `{content}`, but settings can accept additional placeholders and schema import can copy them from Roam. A format such as `EVD - {content} - {Source}` then makes import fall back to the original title.
* Source information already has a separate relation path through [ENG-2140](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2140>).

>>>

>>> ## Solution

* When constructing Obsidian titles on import, replace unsupported placeholders with an empty string. Keep the surrounding literal text and separators.
* Apply the same title-construction behavior to local node creation and import, including existing formats.
* [ENG-2323](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2323>) covers the inline warning during manual node type creation or editing. This ticket covers title construction for those same formats. Import does not add placeholder warnings or notices.

>>>

>>> ## Done When

* With `core_title` set to `REM sleep aids recall`, the formatting result for `EVD - {content} - {Source}` is `EVD - REM sleep aids recall - `. The trailing separator remains; existing filename trimming still applies. Unsupported placeholders do not trigger an incoming-title fallback, appear literally, or produce regex text.
* Tests cover `{Source}`, an arbitrary unsupported placeholder, multiple unsupported placeholders, preservation of surrounding literal text, and unchanged content-only formats. Missing `{content}` remains invalid.
* Local node creation and import use the same title-construction behavior for existing formats without a bulk migration. Source-relation import remains unchanged.

>>>

>>> ## Out of Scope

* Removing separators or otherwise cleaning up literal formatting around ignored placeholders.
* Final filename sanitization, attachment paths, and bulk rewriting of stored formats or filenames.
* Repairing missing or incorrect `core_title` data, changing its fallback policy, or changing Roam placeholder behavior.

>>>

>>> ## Notes

* Coordinate with [ENG-2195](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2195>), which normalizes invalid characters in imported formats, and [ENG-2157](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2157>), which reconstructs Obsidian titles. The remaining filename/link sanitization discussed in [#1481](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/issues/1481>) and [DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1482](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/derive-obsidian-import-file-names-from-titles-obsidian-can-create-1aae3fd6503b>) (<pull-request id="0a3d4023-d75c-4bdf-a73a-977687bb97cc" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/derive-obsidian-import-file-names-from-titles-obsidian-can-create-1aae3fd6503b">DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1482</pull-request>) is outside v0 scope.
* Relevant paths: `createNode.ts` and `importNodes.ts`. The decorator in `packages/database/src/lib/decorateTitle.ts` is shared with Roam; preserve Roam behavior.
* Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style

I'm looking at ENG-2346, which flags that missing content remains invalid in DW tests and notes to coordinate with ENG-2195. It also references PR #1482 about deriving Obsidian import filenames from titles, so I want to check whether that PR is still open and whether it touches the sanitizeFileName logic in importNodes.ts.

Checking the open PR list, #1482 doesn't appear among those touching importNodes.ts or validateNodeType.ts, so it's likely closed or affects different files — not critical to the decision at hand.

Weighing Fork A versus Fork B for ENG-2195, I conclude ENG-2346's statement about missing content staying invalid refers to validation not being loosened, not to import-time repair, so Fork B's fallback behavior at import doesn't actually conflict with it. I'm leaning toward recommending a minimal version of Fork B.

My recommendation is to prevent the uniqueness regression by falling back to a name-derived default when the normalized format fails validation against the vault's node types, canonicalizing `{Content}` to `{content}` first, and keeping the default even if it also fails as a documented residual case. I'm weighing whether this fallback naming produces acceptable UX — it would still be distinguishable from colliding local types, and since auto-merging isn't a goal, that's fine. I'm now working through a concrete collision scenario comparing Roam's and Obsidian's default node type formats for Claim, Question, Evidence, and Source to stress-test this approach.

Collisions only arise when a user has renamed a node type locally while keeping the same format string as an imported type with a different name — that's rare but real, and it's genuinely new harm introduced by this PR that the fallback approach in Fork B would resolve, versus Fork A which would just document the limitation. I still need sid's decision on two open points: whether to go with Fork A or the minimal Fork B fix, and whether to address the specImport create/merge path now or defer it with a ticket, since exported spec files from vaults that pre-PR imported Roam types could contain stale format strings that cause issues on reimport.

That commit likely predates the ticket itself, and the ticket's language about "imported schemas" persisting Roam formats like `[[CLM]] - {content}` points specifically to cross-space imports from Supabase, whereas the spec files I'm looking at come through Obsidian exports instead.

I'm weighing whether to include a normalization fix here or defer it with a follow-up ticket — it's a small addition (~4 lines) that would close a real gap a reviewer would likely flag, since the merge path writes onto a local editable type and an incoming format chosen for merge would need normalization too.

But then thinking about Fork B's uniqueness fallback for specImport feels like it overlaps with the import modal's own conflict resolution, which gets complicated fast. That complexity pushes me toward deferring specImport to keep this PR scoped to the cross-space schema import boundary, so I'll recommend deferring D2 and present that reasoning to sid along with the Fork B-minimal approach.

The reviewer's draft reply to Michael about duplication is outward-facing on Linear under sid's identity, so I'd rather include it as a draft in my message to sid for him to approve and post rather than posting it myself. I also notice Michael's note that sid is now the assignee, likely auto-assigned via the PR link, which is just an observation to pass along.

For the remaining fix-ups: normalizing the name-derived default is a one-line change under Fork B since the fallback needs normalizing regardless. The comment wording and test title fixes depend on which fork wins, with Fork B needing added test cases. The trickier issue is the test for the removed call — ENG-2351 already has an untracked test file with its own harness, so I don't want to duplicate that; better to add a format assertion once ENG-2351 lands, though that creates an awkward cross-PR dependency. Under Fork B, since the validation logic moves into the node-type-mapping function, I'd need a pure helper to test the settings-dependent resolution path without relying on the other PR's harness.

I'm deciding whether to block on sid's answer for the D1 fork choice before applying the ENG-2195 fixes, since the fork affects how P3-1 merges — safest is to wait on D1 while other non-fork-dependent work (P3-1, P3-2, the body reason fix with deferral, ENG-2346 citation) proceeds in parallel. I'm now considering whether to raise D1 and D2 as explicit questions to the user.

AskUserQuestion could block my turn if the user is away, which would stall processing of other agents' completions while I wait. I'd rather post the open question in my final message and end the turn, letting agent notifications re-invoke me so I keep progressing on other threads until sid actually replies.

Since I'm only blocked on ENG-2195's fork and other streams can proceed, I'll move forward: send ENG-2348 test addition to implementer a913c6f959d09140b (jsdom render test modeled on tentativeRelationLoading.test.ts, update PR body testing note, push), then re-run reviewer ae8465581b29085b2 in re-review mode against SHA 01816bcf, and log these decisions in the state file.
ENG-2346 confirms missing `{content}` stays invalid and its notes point to coordinating with ENG-2195, so that decision is on us. Next, I'll check the ENG-2348 test.
